classification.difficultyReason: Part a scaffolds conversion of the percentage threshold into 8, 9 or 10 heads; part b then requires a routine three-term binomial sum.

content.prompt: A coin is tossed 10 times, and a student is asked to calculate the probability that more than 75% of the coins will show heads.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If more than 75% of the coins show heads, how many coins would this be?

answer.worked: $75\%$ of $10$ is $7.5$. More than $7.5$ heads means 8, 9 or 10 heads.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use the binomial probability formula to determine the probability of obtaining more than 75% heads. On this occasion the calculation is easily done without a normal approximation.

answer.worked:
Let $X$ be the number of heads. Then $X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(10,0.5)$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X\ge8)&=P(X=8)+P(X=9)+P(X=10)\\P(X\ge8)&=\frac{\binom{10}{8}+\binom{10}{9}+\binom{10}{10}}{2^{10}}\\P(X\ge8)&=\frac{45+10+1}{1024}\\P(X\ge8)&=\frac7{128}\\P(X\ge8)&\approx0.0547=5.47\%.\end{aligned}$$
